name: Vigil
author: Marc Ferro @keasbeexd
description: A security suite for Omarchy in five pillars: hardening, malware detection (with ClamUI), supply-chain checks (with Bumblebee), privacy and system care. Plain-language findings and fixes you approve one by one; root changes ask for your password. No telemetry: it only contacts the sources it checks against.

barWidget.description: Security score in the bar; Harden, Detect, Supply, Privacy and Care tabs in the panel

schema.label: Check every (minutes)
schema.description: How often Vigil reads your settings and files again in the background (it also does whenever you open the panel): read-only, no network, well under a second.

schema.label: Notify about new findings
schema.description: Send one desktop notification when a check that was fine starts failing. The notification only says how many; details stay in the panel.

schema.label: Background checks
schema.description: Runs the daily and weekly checks by themselves. Every scan gets its list right before it runs. Daily: waiting system and Flatpak updates; known vulnerabilities (arch-audit downloads the tracker from security.archlinux.org); known-malicious npm and Bun packages (osv-scanner sends package names and versions to OSV.dev, never files); your AUR packages (aur.archlinux.org); Perplexity's Bumblebee list from GitHub, then a Bumblebee scan; and a ClamAV scan of what is new in Downloads. Weekly: firmware (LVFS) and a ClamAV scan of your home folder. Each step runs only once its tool is installed; scans run as you, and the background run never asks for a password. Turn off to run them only with the Run now buttons.
